outcome_detail: Federal lawsuit reported as newly filed in May 2026; no responsive rulings, settlement, or judgment reported as of July 2026. The parallel criminal case against the former officer was also still pending in available coverage.
criminal_detail: Justice Feeley-Carim, 30, turned himself in at the Palm Beach County Main Detention Center on August 30, 2025 on charges of false imprisonment, simple battery, and misuse of official position stemming from the March 26, 2025 Walmart parking lot incident. He had been fired April 16, 2025 while on probationary status. His attorney says he 'vehemently denies these false accusations.' No plea or trial outcome reported as of July 2026.
description: A 38-year-old woman, proceeding as Jane Doe, filed a federal lawsuit against the City of West Palm Beach, reported in May 2026, over an alleged March 26, 2025 incident involving then-rookie police officer Justice Feeley-Carim. According to the lawsuit and the related arrest report, Feeley-Carim used his marked patrol car to block in a parked car at a Walmart on 45th Street, detained the woman for about 20 minutes, made sexual advances, and ordered her to touch him sexually, which she says she did out of fear of arrest. The suit alleges city leaders fostered 'a culture of lawlessness' in the police department and showed deliberate indifference, noting that internal affairs had already received two complaints about Feeley-Carim before the incident. Feeley-Carim was fired in April 2025 and criminally charged in August 2025 with false imprisonment, simple battery, and misuse of official position; he denies the allegations. The civil case is in its early stages.
